alternativeSelection.assessment: The first option balances business, mathematics and computing. The second puts more weight on algorithms and mathematical models. The third applies analytics to markets, finance and strategy. The three options differ by at least four courses in each direction. Responsible AI is a further interest and appears within the first and third options through study of AI governance.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to Probability Theory and Statistics 1.
Both study the pricing of financial assets and the role of risk. UCR also examines banking and monetary policy.
Both examine responsible uses of AI in organisations. UvA also studies data privacy and cybersecurity directly.
UvA develops consulting skills for analytics work in organisations.
Both use regression and statistical inference to estimate economic relationships and make predictions.
Both examine questions about people at work. UCR studies organisational behaviour, while UvA uses HR data to answer those questions.
Both use financial statements and accounting information to assess performance.
Both study venture opportunities, customer needs and business models. UvA applies them in a hackathon.
UvA offers a minor, an exchange, electives or an internship combined with electives. The UvA Business Analytics internship carries 12 EC and requires 90 EC already completed.
Both study customer evidence to inform marketing. UvA specifically teaches purchase prediction, choice and marketing-mix models.
UvA requires this 6 EC project alongside the 6 EC Skills course. UCR’s optional research element sits outside the illustrated schedules.
This 6 EC course develops design research and thesis writing alongside the Research Project.
Both develop differentiation and integration for mathematical modelling.
Both cover matrices, linear systems, vector spaces and eigenvalues.
Both develop probability distributions and statistical inference. UvA teaches these topics across two courses.
UvA requires a second linear algebra course. UCR covers some related topics in Linear Algebra, including eigenvalues and orthogonality.
Both teach linear and discrete optimisation. UvA develops operations research models, while UCR also studies search in AI.
UvA devotes a course to modelling uncertain operations. UCR teaches probabilistic decisions in AI, but has no equivalent operations research sequence in these options.
UvA introduces optimisation and machine learning together through cases about social problems.
Both develop Python programming and computational problem solving.
UvA devotes a course to visualising and communicating results. UCR includes visualisation in Introduction to Data Science.
Both prepare and explore data for analysis. UCR also practises data visualisation.
Both study data structures, efficient algorithms and computational problem solving.
Both cover regression, classification, feature engineering and model evaluation.
Both use models for text classification and generation. UvA also teaches retrieval, while UCR covers image and time-series applications.
Both cover databases. UvA places data management alongside enterprise systems and other digital technologies.

audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options explore a balance of business and analytics, a technical focus on algorithms and AI, or a business focus on markets and finance.
